cues.text: A tag in the wrong place can ruin a garment. These are the most common mistakes, and how to avoid them.
Stapling into silk or satin. The holes never close. Use a safety pin on the label.
Stapling into leather, suede, or vinyl. The holes are permanent. Pin to the label only.
Stapling into a sweater or knit. It pulls threads and makes runs. Use a safety pin.
Stapling through two layers, like the lining and the outside of a jacket. It puckers and tears.
Metal staples can rust in wash and press, and leave an orange stain. Keep staples in the label and small.
A tag on the outside of the garment can leave a shiny mark after pressing.
A messy or wrong number sends the garment to the wrong customer. Write clearly, and check it against the ticket.
Forgetting one piece, like the pants of a suit. That piece gets lost.
When you take a tag off, use a staple remover and pull straight out, slowly.
Never rip a tag off. It can tear the label, or even the garment.
If you ever make a hole or a snag, stop and tell a manager right away. Do not hide it. It is often fixable if we catch it early.
